newsitem.title: USA: Conn. Gov. Rowland lags in election poll.
newsitem.headline: Conn. Gov. Rowland lags in election poll.

text.p: Connecticut Gov. John Rowland (R) lags behind U.S. Rep. Barbara Kennelly (D) in a hypothetical 1998 gubernatorial election contest, according to a Hartford Courant/Connecticut Poll published on Wednesday.
The poll also shows U.S. Sen. Christopher Dodd (D) in a stronger starting position for re-election next year than Rowland.

In the survey, Kennelly led Rowland by 40 percent to 36 percent, with 24 percent not responding. The poll has a margin of error of plus or minus five percentage points, which means that Kennelly's four-point lead is not necessarily decisive.
Still, it is significant for Kennelly to be rated neck-and-neck at this early stage, since she has not yet made up her mind whether to seek the governor's seat, the Courant said.

Poll director G. Donald Ferree said that the results indicate "base-line strength" for Kennelly, but cautioned that "it would be dangerous to interpret these numbers as what would happen if the election were being held today."
He said Kennelly looked stronger than the other Democrats who were individually matched up in a hypothetical race against Rowland.
Those other Democrats included the three most prominently mentioned: 1994 nominee Bill Curry, Bridgeport Mayor Joseph Ganim and House Speaker Thomas Ritter.
Of the 500 randomly selected residents throughout the state, some 37 percent said they would like to see Rowland re-elected, while 44 percent said they would "like someone else."

Ferree said it is still early and experience shows Rowland is not necessarily in trouble. The poll does not mean that 44 percent of the voters are against Rowland, but that they are open to an alternative, he said.
Some 48 percent said they would like to see Dodd re-elected senator, while 33 percent said "someone else."
Dodd did well in a hypothetical match-up against Connecticut Treasurer Christopher Burnham (R), who is considering a run against Dodd next year. Dodd led Burnham 49 percent to 19 percent.
